restrictions: Two distinct 64-byte messages with equal digests for the Orchard hash with 23 partial rounds (poseidon-orchard-r23-prefix-v1), found as a collision F(x) = F(y), x != y, of the walk F(x) = digest(message(x + rho0)) / OUTSCALE: message() is the injective parametrisation of the input line on which rounds 0 and 1 are affine, OUTSCALE a fixed nonzero field constant, rho0 a random 254-bit coin of the attempt. Plain birthday search, one trail with distinguished points, one table; the success probability uses no property of the rounds.

Cost model orchard-field-ram-v2, C = 699. Prices used: canonical field ADD and MUL 1/C each; every other primitive 256-bit word operation (AND, OR, shift, compare, branch, register move, aligned load or store, random word) 1/C. No permutation call is charged as a unit: every evaluation executes the 412-operation step program (165 ADD, 247 MUL; proof.md Section 3, listing in Appendix B), an equivalent form of rounds 2-63 that equals the reference digest divided by OUTSCALE. Constant loads: the 162 step constants are loaded once per attempt (162 loads, charged) into a declared file of 223 256-bit registers, counted in memory; arithmetic takes register operands.

Ledger (proof.md Section 7, instruction listings): a trail step is 412 + 3 operations, plus 3 per block of 8 unrolled steps (415.375 per step); a recovery evaluation at most 412 + 6; table scan, insertion, bisection, constant loads, the message roots and setup are at most 12,407,219,109 operations. The offline derivation of the step constants and fixed parameters (build_step, tune.py in exact integer arithmetic, one run of plan) is bounded by 186,527,993,160 word operations from the metered counts of the shipped code (proof.md Section 9); that bound is inside time_log2 and is also declared as preprocessing_log2 = 28 (one quantity, not added twice). time_log2 is the full budget with every halt charged at its limit: S = n + d trail steps and 3 gmax recovery evaluations, n = 133566495 * 2^100 (log2 126.9930), d = 64944601529831955217415195487821408, gmax = 135016408443598012162521064303628701.

Memory: 25,554 table entries of one 32-byte word (high 126 bits of the value OR index), a side array of 16-bit low parts (1,598 words), the start word, code at most 4,517 instructions at 36 bytes, constants and the 223-register file: 1,044,180 bytes, below 2^20 (proof.md Section 8); the normalized memory penalty is zero and memory_log2_bytes = 20.

Success probability at least 0.39: Lemma 2 (proof.md Section 5) proves 0.39000000244948219830 (at least 0.39) for a uniformly random function at the filed budget, in exact integer arithmetic, with explicit terms for the trail, detection, table and gaps. H1 (the only premise, score-critical, our theory that the fixed map behaves like a uniformly random function for this search) states that the real map with the random coin rho0 reaches 0.39 at the filed budget; measurements of the real r=23 map family are cited in proof.md Section 6.

The program is printed in full in proof.md Appendix A (standard library only); the step program in Appendix B. One organizer-run experiment is declared (lowbits-birthday, python-message-pairs-v1, event digest-xor-mask; source experiments/exp_lowbits.py, round-parameterized from the intake request): agreement of the first 14 bits of this target's own digest. No full collision is produced or claimed; the claim is the cost of the search.

heuristics.statement: The filed trail has n = 133566495 * 2^100 steps, at which Lemma 2 gives 0.390000002 for a uniformly random function (the least multiple of 2^100 that reaches 0.39). Premise: for the attempt's coins rho0 and x_0 (uniform 254-bit words), the search of proof.md Section 4 on the real map F(x) = digest(message(x + rho0)) / OUTSCALE, at the budget n, succeeds with probability at least 0.39. H1 is our theory that, for this search, the fixed map behaves like a uniformly random function.
heuristics.scope: Target poseidon-orchard-r23-prefix-v1, inputs on the line of proof.md Section 2, one trail with the parameters of proof.md Section 4 (S = 1.6938e38 evaluations). Applies to this round count and budget. Only the success probability rests on it; the step program, the recovery, the ledger and the memory are proved or checked exactly (proof.md Sections 3, 4, 7, 8, 11).
heuristics.extrapolation: Organizer-run experiment lowbits-birthday (python-message-pairs-v1, digest-xor-mask, 256 trials; proof.md Section 10): regime = this target's own digest at r = 23, agreement of the first 14 bits, fresh random inputs, at most 1200 evaluations per trial (a random function needs about 160); the real digest returns a verified pair in every trial, as a random 14-bit function does. Cited participant-run measurements on the same map family: the 16,380-walk first-repeat campaign of our r=23 entry a5a40e52 on the truncated r=23 map (widths 16..36, fresh (rho, start) per walk, exact discrete likelihood, pooled hazard 1.0044, profile-likelihood 95% interval [0.9891, 1.0198]; the walked map is bit-identical to this entry's, proof.md Section 6), and the r = 7, 23, 56 truncated-output campaigns of the dependency bf6d2b58.
heuristics.limitations: H1 concerns the average over the attempt's coin rho0, which is what Lemma 2 bounds. Evidence: the cited measurements (outputs of 16 to 40 bits, trails of at most 2,970,429 steps) and the experiment of Section 10; none of them reaches the filed width, and the premise is not a proof.
